mainEntity.name: How much does a Range Rover P400 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A complete rebuilt Range Rover P400 engine typically costs between £6,500 and £10,000 for supply only [EM-QUOTE]. Used units start from around £2,500. Reconditioned units range from £4,500 to £7,500. Prices vary based on the specific AJ20P6 engine code and supplier.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of cooling or timing chain failure in a Range Rover P400?

acceptedAnswer.text: Early warning signs include unexplained coolant loss, a sweet smell from the engine bay, or a distinct rattling noise during cold starts. Dashboard warning lights for engine temperature or low coolant. Loss of low-end torque or hesitation under acceleration. Metallic debris in the engine oil (in severe timing chain cases).

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Range Rover P400?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, absolutely. The Range Rover P400 is a high-value luxury SUV with current market values ranging from £75,000 to over £120,000 [THIRD-PARTY]. A rebuilt engine cost is a small fraction of the vehicle's total value. It preserves the car's performance, refinement, and resale value. Upgraded rebuilt units address known factory cooling and timing weaknesses.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Range Rover P400 engine supply and fit take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional Range Rover P400 engine replacement typically takes 3 to 5 working days. Removal and preparation of the old unit takes 1-2 days. Fitting, calibration, and 48V MHEV system testing of the new rebuilt engine takes 2-3 days. Nationwide collection and delivery are arranged by the specialist.

mainEntity.name: Do rebuilt P400 engines retain the 48V mild-hybrid (MHEV) functionality?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, reputable specialists rebuilding a Range Rover P400 engine ensure full compatibility with the 48V mild-hybrid architecture. The electric supercharger and integrated starter-generator (ISG) are tested and calibrated. All MHEV software maps are retained or updated to factory specifications. This ensures seamless stop-start operation and torque-fill performance.

commonProblems.h2: Range Rover P400 Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The 3.0L Ingenium inline-six in the Range Rover P400 is a complex, high-performance unit. While generally robust, its dual-charging system (electric supercharger + turbo) and cooling architecture require precise maintenance. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, backed by a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Cooling System & Water Pump Vulnerability - Why the Range Rover P400 AJ20P6 Requires Attention
problems.rootCause: Plastic coolant crossover pipes and electric water pump components can degrade under repeated heat cycles, leading to coolant loss and potential overheating if not addressed promptly.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Coolant flush, electric water pump inspection, and seal replacement
repairOptions.longevity: Highly suitable for minor leaks before overheating occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of a rebuilt 3.0L I6 with upgraded cooling components and 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary if coolant loss has caused severe overheating and warped components

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Range Rover P400 holds a current UK market value of £75,000-£120,000+ depending on specification and mileage [THIRD-PARTY]. At this valuation, a rebuilt engine replacement cost represents a small fraction of the vehicle's total value, making professional replacement highly viable to preserve its premium status.
problems.recommendation: Proactive replacement of the electric water pump and coolant crossover pipes is a highly recommended, low-cost preventative measure. If overheating has already occurred, a full rebuilt engine replacement is the safest and most reliable solution to protect your investment.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt AJ20P6 Range Rover P400 engine prices

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner & Dual-Charging Wear - Range Rover P400 Performance Vulnerability
problems.rootCause: The complex timing chain arrangement and electric supercharger isolator coupler can experience wear over time, leading to rattling on cold starts or a loss of low-end torque.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Inspection and replacement of chain tensioners, guides, and supercharger coupler
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if the engine block and internals are undamaged

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of a rebuilt engine with upgraded tensioner components and 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if catastrophic failure has occurred or the block is compromised

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Given the £75,000-£120,000+ value band of the Range Rover P400, addressing timing chain wear early is trivial compared to the vehicle's worth. Ignoring it risks catastrophic failure, making a rebuilt engine the necessary fallback if damage is done.
problems.recommendation: If caught early, a specialist timing chain and supercharger coupler service is the most cost-effective route. However, if the engine has suffered catastrophic failure due to neglected chain wear, investing in a fully rebuilt unit is the only way to guarantee long-term reliability.
